blocks.title: Podcast: “Why Should the Sun Rise Tomorrow?”
paras: **Welcome back.** Today: David Hume and the problem of induction. **Picture this.** The sun has risen every morning of your life. **Do you know** it will rise tomorrow? Hume says: **not strictly**. All our expectations about the future **rest on** the assumption that the future will **resemble** the past. But that assumption **cannot itself be proved** without **going in a circle**.

**Here’s the twist.** Hume doesn’t tell us to **stop expecting** sunrises. He says expectation is the work of **custom**, not reason. **Think of** billiard balls: we see one strike another, then motion; we never see the **necessary connexion**. **So**, what we call causation **is a habit of the mind**. **That’s the puzzle**; **next time**, how Kant answered it.

items.q: Hume says we know strictly that the sun will rise.

items.why: the work of custom, not reason.

items.q: Kant’s answer is explained in this episode.

blocks.body: Em podcasts, frases curtas e **marcadores de voz** guiam a atenção. A entonação oscila mais: sobe nas perguntas (↗) e **desce firme** quando o locutor entrega a inferência (↘).
*Strictly* tem sentido de “rigorosamente”: *not strictly* = “não de modo rigoroso”.

blocks.title: Match the word to its meaning

body: **Picture this.** — Imagine só.
**Here’s the twist.** — Eis a reviravolta.
**Out of habit.** — Por hábito.
**Rest on.** — Basear-se em.
**Go in circles.** — Andar em círculos.
**Take it on trust.** — Aceitar por confiança.
**Once bitten, twice shy.** — Gato escaldado.
**As sure as eggs.** — Certo como dois e dois.
**Past performance.** — Desempenho passado.
**A leap of faith.** — Salto de fé.
**And that is the puzzle.** — E esse é o enigma.
**Do you know the sun will rise tomorrow?** — Você sabe que o sol vai nascer amanhã?
**Not strictly. I expect it out of habit.** — Não rigorosamente. Espero por hábito.

blocks.task: Write a 6-sentence podcast intro on a puzzle you like, using Picture this, a rhetorical question and Here’s the twist.

Use exemplos reais da vida dos alunos e peça frases próprias.
